articles.headline: datasette-llm 0.1a9 drops – default model auto‑pick added, scaling hints, and Snapdragon slowdown warning
articles.dek: Version 0.1a9 of the datasette-llm plugin ships with a built‑in default model selector, new discovery tags, and a heads‑up that Snapdragon X2 Elite drivers can shave up to 87% off LLM speed.

body.text: Key Takeaway

datasette-llm 0.1a9 adds an automatic default model selector for the Datasette Agent, includes new tags for easier discovery, and references recent scaling strategies—all while Snapdragon X2 Elite users see up to 87% slower LLM performance after a driver update [FACT:b59d1d20ddafbbc5d5787a22453415d3][FACT:61e62247b2f2d920179450c6b57245ff][FACT:e3fa9f0712b50f9241563ae46b7b37d6][FACT:608b1df15638d1ac1932c7fdfb4d14fb][FACT:fd107a3ea76ca872ad7e5d00880c3c1c].
Why This Matters

Builders can now drop the manual model‑selection step, saving configuration time, but they should audit their hardware because the same driver that shipped with Snapdragon X2 Elite can cripple LLM throughput [FACT:61e62247b2f2d920179450c6b57245ff][FACT:fd107a3ea76ca872ad7e5d00880c3c1c].
What Happened

On Oct 31 2026 Simon Willison released datasette‑llm 0.1a9; the package bumps the core plugin version, adds the ‘default model’ flag to the agent, and ships with metadata tags ‘datasette‑llm’ and ‘datasette‑agent’ to help tooling discover it [FACT:b59d1d20ddafbbc5d5787a22453415d3][FACT:e3fa9f0712b50f9241563ae46b7b37d6]. The announcement also links to a broader discussion on scaling multi‑agent orchestration, reminding users that LLM pipelines still hit bottlenecks as they grow [FACT:608b1df15638d1ac1932c7fdfb4d14fb].
Builder View

If you run a small internal API, set the new default‑model flag and let the agent pick the first available model; for larger deployments, benchmark the chosen model against your Snapdragon‑based edge nodes because the latest driver update has been reported to cut LLM speed by nearly 90% [FACT:61e62247b2f2d920179450c6b57245ff][FACT:fd107a3ea76ca872ad7e5d00880c3c1c].
Open Questions

How much faster the built‑in default model is compared with custom selections, and whether the scaling guidance will be reflected in future plugin releases, remain open; also, the Snapdragon slowdown may be driver‑specific, so we need official numbers from the chip vendor [FACT:608b1df15638d1ac1932c7fdfb4d14fb][FACT:fd107a3ea76ca872ad7e5d00880c3c1c].
Ardur Take

Two independent reports confirm the version bump and the hardware issue, so we rate confidence as high; the practical impact is immediate for anyone using Datasette Agent, but the performance warning is a reminder to test on target hardware before go‑live [FACT:b59d1d20ddafbbc5d5787a22453415d3][FACT:fd107a3ea76ca872ad7e5d00880c3c1c].

keyPoints: datasette-llm 0.1a9 introduces a default‑model flag that auto‑selects a model for the agent.
New tags ‘datasette‑llm’ and ‘datasette‑agent’ improve plugin discoverability.
Scaling discussion highlights ongoing multi‑agent orchestration bottlenecks.
Snapdragon X2 Elite driver update can slow LLM inference by up to 87%.
articles.whyItMatters: The default‑model feature cuts a common manual step, letting teams spin up LLM‑backed APIs faster, while the scaling notes remind architects that growth still brings coordination costs. At the same time, the Snapdragon performance hit could invalidate edge‑deployment plans unless hardware or drivers are vetted.
articles.readerAction: Upgrade to datasette‑llm 0.1a9, enable the default‑model flag in your Datasette Agent config, and run a quick latency benchmark on any Snapdragon‑based nodes; if you see a slowdown, consider rolling back the driver or switching to a supported GPU.
